newsitem.title: GERMANY: Adidas shares drop on rumoured downgrades.
newsitem.headline: Adidas shares drop on rumoured downgrades.

text.p: Shares in German sportswear manufacturer Adidas dropped on Friday as dealers reported rumours that certain banks had downgraded their earnings outlooks for the firm.
Adidas lost almost seven percent at one point, falling 9.80 marks to 133 marks. Later it recouped some ground to trade at 136.50 marks at 1012 GMT.
Dealers said the stock, which rose recently after it said it would be an official sponsor of the 1998 soccer World Cup, was not being seen as positively as before by certain banks.
"There are rumours that earnings downgrades are in the pipeline," said one trader.

"There are rumours that some of the earnings estimates that are in the market are too high, but I don't think any fundamental analysis has yet been done on the reason for those rumours," said one analyst.

Deutsche Bank and Schroeder, Munchmeyer, Hengst & Co denied they had changed their recommendations and nobody at Goldman Sachs was immediately available for comment on talk it had downgraded the company.
"There has been additional pressure from the catastrophic Reebok figures," said another analyst.
U.S. sportswear firm Reebok closed Wall Street trade down 5/8 at $33-3/4 on Thursday after it said it expects continued pressure in its footwear sales and gross margins in 1997.
Worldwide sales of Reebok brand products fell 2.9 percent in the third quarter to $834.8 million, the company said.
